title: Electromagnetic Waves
seo_title: Electromagnetic Waves Class 12 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 8)
standard_text: Basic idea of displacement current, electromagnetic waves, their characteristics, their transverse nature (qualitative idea only). Electromagnetic spectrum (radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays) including elementary facts about their uses.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 8 Electromagnetic Waves: displacement current, properties of EM waves, c = fλ, E₀ = cB₀, and the uses of each part of the electromagnetic spectrum. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Radio → microwave → IR → visible → UV → X-ray → gamma: λ gets shorter.
body_html:
How to think about it

Maxwell added the displacement current, due to a changing electric field, and predicted electromagnetic waves: oscillating E and B fields, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel, moving at c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) = 3 × 10⁸ m/s, with E₀ = cB₀.

The electromagnetic spectrum runs from radio waves (longest wavelength) through microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet and X-rays to gamma rays (shortest). Each has its uses, from broadcasting to radiotherapy.

Example

λ = 3 m. f?

3 × 10⁸ ÷ 3

Answer: 10⁸ Hz

Example

Used in remote controls?

heat waves

Answer: infrared

Common mistakes

  • Thinking EM waves need a medium.
  • Mixing up the order of the spectrum.
  • Saying E and B are parallel.
